newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-SHERIYAR SPOILS FIRST PART OF GOOCH FAREWELL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SHERIYAR SPOILS FIRST PART OF GOOCH FAREWELL.

text.p: Graham Gooch's hopes of making a spectacular farewell from England cricket were upset by Worcestershire paceman Alamgir Sheriyar in the English county championship on Thursday.
Former England captain Gooch was desperate to finish his career with a big score on his home ground in his penultimate innings for Essex at Chelmsford.
But the 44-year-old had made only 11 from 26 balls before losing his leg stump to Sheriyar after making room to try and force the ball through mid-wicket.
Sheriyar showed no mercy for one of the England's most popular cricketing figures.
He promised that he would be looking for a repeat performance when Gooch steps out for his final innings either on Friday or Saturday.
"He is a great player and it is always nice to get someone out who has scored so many Test runs and played that many years," he said.
"I was there to do a job. I know it could be very emotional when Graham goes to the wicket for the last time but I'll be trying to do the same as in the first innings.
"That's what I'm paid to do and we need a win. It's first-class cricket and it is never an arena where you are going to throw freebies to someone just because he is retiring."
Essex went on to finish the second day of the four-day clash on 230 for three, still trailing Worcestershire's 394 all out.
Championship leaders Glamorgan have plenty to do if they are to stay out in front after seeing Derbyshire bat on to make 513 for six before the declaration finally came at Chesterfield.
Glamorgan then lost their in-form batsman Steve James for 25 out of 39 for one before the end of a rain-hit day.
